items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Triangulation.
o: a triangle whose angles are close to sixty degrees, giving reliable positions
the height of a point above or below a chosen datum
a blunder such as a misread figure that cannot be adjusted out later
the method of fixing positions by measuring angles or sides of a network of triangles
items.s: Triangulation: the method of fixing positions by measuring angles or sides of a network of triangles. The other options describe Well conditioned triangle, Reduced level, Mistake.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Peg.
o: the levelling reduction in which successive readings are compared to find rises and falls
the deviation of the magnetic needle caused by nearby iron or electric currents
the short wooden stake driven in to mark a station
the sighting rule used with a plane table to draw directions
items.s: Peg: the short wooden stake driven in to mark a station. The other options describe Rise and fall method, Alidade, Local attraction.

o: a triangle whose angles are close to sixty degrees, giving reliable positions
the satellite system that gives position anywhere on earth from signals
a line measured to confirm that the framework of a survey is correct
surveying that allows for the curvature of the earth over large areas
items.s: Global positioning system: the satellite system that gives position anywhere on earth from signals. The other options describe Well conditioned triangle, Check line, Geodetic surveying.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Working from the whole to the part?
o: a survey that defines boundaries of land parcels for ownership records
the surveying principle of fixing a larger frame accurately before filling in detail
the levelling reduction in which successive readings are compared to find rises and falls
a survey in which the framework is made up of triangles measured with a chain or tape
items.s: Working from the whole to the part: the surveying principle of fixing a larger frame accurately before filling in detail. The other options describe Chain surveying, Rise and fall method, Cadastral survey.

the deviation of the magnetic needle caused by nearby iron or electric currents
the reduced level of the line of sight of the instrument
a bearing measured clockwise from true north
items.s: Height of collimation: the reduced level of the line of sight of the instrument. The other options describe True bearing, Photogrammetry, Local attraction.

a bearing measured clockwise from true north
the bearing of a line viewed in the opposite direction from its forward bearing
the pointed marking pin used to count chain lengths along a line
items.s: Back bearing: the bearing of a line viewed in the opposite direction from its forward bearing. The other options describe True bearing, Arrow, Chain surveying.

a survey that locates natural and artificial features and shows them with contours
a survey in which the framework is made up of triangles measured with a chain or tape
items.s: Error: the difference between a measured value and its true value. The other options describe Chain surveying, Topographic survey, Magnetic declination.

a survey that locates natural and artificial features and shows them with contours
an error that tends to cancel out over a series of measurements

Local attraction
Traverse
True bearing
items.s: Traverse is a series of connected lines whose lengths and directions are measured.

items.q: In this course, Magnetic bearing refers to
o: a bearing measured clockwise from true north
the instrument for measuring horizontal and vertical angles accurately
a bearing measured clockwise from magnetic north
the angle between magnetic north and true north at a place
items.s: Magnetic bearing: a bearing measured clockwise from magnetic north. The other options describe Theodolite, Magnetic declination, True bearing.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Triangulation.
o: a survey in which the framework is made up of triangles measured with a chain or tape
a triangle whose angles are close to sixty degrees, giving reliable positions
the method of fixing positions by measuring angles or sides of a network of triangles
a triangle with a very small angle, giving unreliable positions
items.s: Triangulation: the method of fixing positions by measuring angles or sides of a network of triangles. The other options describe Ill conditioned triangle, Chain surveying, Well conditioned triangle.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Bench mark.
o: a staff reading taken between the back sight and the fore sight
the reduced level of the line of sight of the instrument
a permanent mark of known reduced level
a line joining points of equal height on a map
items.s: Bench mark: a permanent mark of known reduced level. The other options describe Contour, Height of collimation, Intermediate sight.

items.q: “the closeness of repeated measurements to one another” is the definition of
o: Cumulative error
Control point
Check line
Precision
items.s: Precision is the closeness of repeated measurements to one another.

items.q: The correct meaning of Magnetic declination is
o: a bearing measured clockwise from true north
the angle between magnetic north and true north at a place
the deviation of the magnetic needle caused by nearby iron or electric currents
a series of connected lines whose lengths and directions are measured
items.s: Magnetic declination: the angle between magnetic north and true north at a place. The other options describe True bearing, Traverse, Local attraction.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Ranging rod.
o: an offset measured at any angle to the survey line, usually when a right angle is impossible
the short wooden stake driven in to mark a station
the instrument used to set out a line at right angles to the chain line
the painted pole used to mark stations and keep measurements in line
items.s: Ranging rod: the painted pole used to mark stations and keep measurements in line. The other options describe Cross staff, Oblique offset, Peg.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Chain surveying.
o: the method of fixing positions by measuring angles or sides of a network of triangles
a triangle with a very small angle, giving unreliable positions
a survey in which the framework is made up of triangles measured with a chain or tape
a triangle whose angles are close to sixty degrees, giving reliable positions
items.s: Chain surveying: a survey in which the framework is made up of triangles measured with a chain or tape. The other options describe Well conditioned triangle, Triangulation, Ill conditioned triangle.

items.q: The correct meaning of Cross staff is
o: an offset measured at any angle to the survey line, usually when a right angle is impossible
the instrument that sets out a right angle by reflecting the line through glass and mirror
the graduated measuring band of a stated length used in chain surveying
the instrument used to set out a line at right angles to the chain line
items.s: Cross staff: the instrument used to set out a line at right angles to the chain line. The other options describe Optical square, Chain, Oblique offset.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Dumpy level.
o: the fixed telescope level used with a staff to take level readings
the first staff reading taken on a point of known level
the height of a point above or below a chosen datum
the surface to which all levels in a survey are referred
items.s: Dumpy level: the fixed telescope level used with a staff to take level readings. The other options describe Datum, Back sight, Reduced level.

items.q: The correct meaning of Tape is
o: the pointed marking pin used to count chain lengths along a line
the measuring ribbon of steel or fibre used for accurate linear measurement
the perpendicular or oblique distance measured from the survey line to a feature
the painted pole used to mark stations and keep measurements in line
items.s: Tape: the measuring ribbon of steel or fibre used for accurate linear measurement. The other options describe Arrow, Ranging rod, Offset.

items.q: Local attraction may be defined as

the deviation of the magnetic needle caused by nearby iron or electric currents
a bearing measured clockwise from true north

items.q: Surveying may be defined as
o: a survey of the bed and features of a body of water
the science of measuring the earth's surface and setting out positions on it
the collection of information about the ground from sensors carried on aircraft or satellites
the transfer of designed positions and levels from drawings to the ground
items.s: Surveying: the science of measuring the earth's surface and setting out positions on it. The other options describe Hydrographic survey, Setting out, Remote sensing.
